old_title: Everton v Man Utd LIVE: Team news and latest updates from Premier League
new_title: Maitland-Niles grabs last-gasp equaliser on Everton debut vs Man Utd - live reaction
old_text:
Everton host Manchester United in the Premier League as David Moyes faces his former side following a dramatic deadline day that left him short of a striker.
The Toffees saw a late move for striker Folarin Balogun collapse after the transfer window had closed and Everton had already sold star forward Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City and striker Beto to Fiorentina. It leaves Everton with Thierno Barry as their only striker, although Jack Grealish has returned for another loan spell at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.
Everton fans were left in dismay after what had been a promising start to the season, with a home win over Crystal Palace followed by a late draw at Bournemouth, with Manchester United now arriving after Bruno Fernandes inspired Michael Carrick's side to victory over Ipswich at Old Trafford thanks to the captain's hat-trick.
Follow all of the latest from the Premier League clash with our live blog below:
The Folarin Balogun shambles exposes much deeper problems at Everton
Is there something wider at play with Everton? The Folarin Balogun saga is just one part of a bigger issue at the club, Richard Jolly writes:
Everton's Folarin Balogun move collapses as striker walks away from £40m deal
What a strange deadline day it was for Everton, seemingly so close to securing the signing of Folarin Balogun but ultimately finding the striker walked away from a deal. Jamie Braidwood has the story:
Everton vs Manchester United LIVE
A very good morning. Another big day of Premier League action is upon us, with two healthy helpings of football ready to be feasted upon. Arsenal and Chelsea clash a little later but first it is Everton and Manchester United who meet, with the hosts dealing with the fallout from a dramatic and frustrating end to the summer transfer window.
Kick off at the Hill Dickinson Stadium is at 2pm BST.
new_text:
Ainsley Maitland-Niles scored a dream stoppage-time equaliser on his Everton debut to earn a 2-2 draw against Manchester United and lift the mood at the end of a difficult week.
Deadline day ended in disappointment for fans of both clubs but the Toffees' inaction was particularly concerning given Tuesday's botched business left them with a threadbare squad to tackle the Premier League and an unhappy manager.
David Moyes admitted he had "to live with disappointments" and called for Everton players to "muck in", but Sunday looked set to end in further frustration after substitute Benjamin Sesko's 88th-minute header put United on course for a late victory.
Tyrique George's thunderous strike had cancelled out a fine Bryan Mbeumo effort moments earlier but the Slovenia international would not prove United's match-winning substitute for the second time at Hill Dickinson Stadium this year. Instead, deadline-day acquisition Maitland-Niles came off the bench to rifle home from distance to snatch a dramatic late point and spark bedlam.
Relive all the action from the Premier League clash with our live blog below:
'Maitland-Niles was worth the wait for Everton fans'
Here's the Sky Sports pundit panel analysing Ainsley Maitland-Niles' late equaliser
Arsenal face Chelsea
As ever, things move quickly in the Premier League. We're straight on to the next game as reigning champions Arsenal host high-flying Chelsea in a potential title race clash?
That game has just got underway and you can follow here:
WATCH: Maitland-Niles' stunning late equaliser
Here's that moment where Ainsley Maitland-Niles snatched a point. A stunning strike
FULL-TIME! Everton 2-2 Man Utd
Her are some of the photos from that Maitland-Niles equaliser...
Maitland-Niles: 'It felt like a win'
"It felt like a win. We dug deep and managed to get a point in the end. The crowd were with us and we were fighting to the end and that's why you get those results," says Maitland-Niles on Sky after the full-time whistle.
"It's amazing, everyone wants to start off like that and thankfully I did. The ball fell to me on the edge of the box, I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I'm happy about.
"I came in to work hard. It's a team full of hard-workers so I fit right in. I'm going to show I can fit right in and pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not more," he added.
FULL-TIME! Everton 2-2 Man Utd
"The point gives you a massive lift if you're Everton. There are players out there capable of living with the best teams. They will battle, and they will work with each other," says former Everton winger pat Nevin on BBC 5 Live.
"In the end, there are going to be injuries. Can you imagine if Jack Grealish picks up another injury? He came on and completely changed the game," he added.
FULL-TIME! Everton 2-2 Man Utd
Two points dropped for Man Utd in what was another disappointing showing in reality. Michael Carrick's changes were surprising and though Sesko made sense as he scored, the visitors ultimately paid the price in what was a pedestrian performance.
As for Everton, that result will raise the mood on Merseyside, and there'll be hope that more can be achieved once their summer signings are fit. Grealish in particular was impressive after coming on.
FULL-TIME! Everton 2-2 Man Utd
"It is beautiful, as soon as he hit it it was going in, what a finish to this game and the 'keeper had no chance," says Lee Hendrie on Sky as the game ends.
